source: J. S. Lewis (1992), PhD thesis, City University London, Table 7.1 (p. 203)
quantity: Axial distance to the first appearance of negative axial velocity
predicted_by: Lewis's own marching finite-difference code (Appendix F), not a measurement
property_basis: inlet bulk (Tb0). Lewis states the ordering by Grq/Re is preserved under mean-bulk (Tbm) and mean-film (Tfm) bases.
note_on_coverage: Table 7.1 lists only the conditions Lewis actually computed for Figures 7.1-7.3, not all 30 runs. A run absent from this table was either not computed or had no reversal predicted within the heated tube; the two are distinguished by the surrounding text, not by the table.

no_reversal_predicted.statement: No flow reversals were predicted within the heated tube for the conditions considered in Figure 7.4.

transcription_check: Gr_q / Re reproduces the printed Gr_q_over_Re for every row to within rounding, which is how the OCR-ambiguous exponents were resolved.

stations_lewis_himself_discounts.x_over_d_0.31_and_0.85: Predictions over-predict Nu here. Lewis attributes this to axial wall conduction preheating the fluid upstream of x=0; he measured the wall at x=0 to be 0.5-5.7 degC above the inlet bulk. No correction was applied in the data reduction.
stations_lewis_himself_discounts.x_over_d_159.33: Lewis calls these values 'suspect': the station sits ~1/3 tube diameter from the end of the heated section and its accuracy 'is also impaired by axial conduction because of heat loss through the adjacent power connection flange'.
